title: SSE: fix streaming chunking/framing for partial JSON & token/event ordering
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Streaming SSE responses for structured output and OpenAI-compatible function/tool calling were intermittently producing malformed partial JSON or out-of-order token/event sequences when high-throughput chunking occurred. This manifested as broken JSON objects in downstream parsers, missing function call metadata, and flaky SDK consumers. Summary: Implement a deterministic framing/state-machine for SSE chunk emission, normalize delimiter handling across runtime and compatibility layers, and enforce token/event ordering guarantees so that "token" events for partially-constructed structured output are emitted consistently before any terminal 'json' or 'done' event. The change set includes runtime fixes, an adapter change in the openai-compat layer, SDK parsing updates, and comprehensive unit/integration tests including a fuzz harness targeting boundary conditions. Backwards compatibility: SSE APIs remain backward compatible for clients that follow the documented OpenAI-compatible framing; edge cases previously producing invalid JSON are now corrected. Performance: microbenchmarks show <3% median latency impact and additional CPU overhead only under pathological chunk boundary workloads. Testing: added unit tests for delimiter normalization, event ordering, and integration tests for function-calling streaming across python/typescript SDKs. Also added CI matrix stress runs to reproduce previous flakes. Related work: addresses ENG-2345 (streaming stability during high-concurrency bursts) and ENG-2378 (function-calling metadata loss in chunked streams).
